name: DOT-Prompt-ProjectNarrative
description: DOT BUILD Grant Project Narrative section - project description, transportation problem, scope, location, and community context

variants.name: default
variants.text:
You are writing the PROJECT NARRATIVE section of a U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) BUILD (Better Utilizing Investments to Leverage Development) Transportation Discretionary Grant application. INPUTS: - {{content}}: The applicant's project documentation, prior studies, community plans, engineering reports, and organizational background. This is your PRIMARY source for all project-specific content. - {{grant_info}}: The specific BUILD NOFO description, including program priorities, eligibility requirements, funding range ($1M-$25M), and any current-year emphasis areas. YOUR TASK: Generate ONLY the Project Narrative section. Do NOT generate the Merit Criteria narrative, Benefit-Cost Analysis, Financial Plan, or other application components. Those are handled separately. NOTE: These prompts are a best-effort starting point. The applicant should review and update all content to reflect their specific project details and the latest BUILD NOFO requirements. ATTRIBUTION REQUIREMENT: Use {{content}} as your primary source and fill in each section as completely as the section structure requires. Whenever a sentence, figure, name, or claim is NOT drawn from {{content}} or {{grant_info}} — including general domain knowledge, typical/illustrative figures, or common practice for similar projects — mark it inline with "[Not sourced from your documents]" immediately after that sentence or list item. This applies to every subsection below, not just cost estimates or statistics specifically. Do not tag section headers or purely structural language. SECTION STRUCTURE: 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW - Provide a concise 2-3 paragraph summary of the project - State the project name, location (city, county, state), and total project cost - Identify the BUILD grant amount requested and the non-federal match (minimum 20% required; note if rural area or historically disadvantaged community qualifies for reduced match) - Identify the lead applicant and any co-applicants or project partners - State the primary transportation mode(s) addressed (road, bridge, transit, rail, port, intermodal, multimodal) - Summarize the core transportation problem being solved in plain language 2. STATEMENT OF NEED - Describe the existing transportation problem or deficiency in specific, quantifiable terms - Include data from {{content}} on current conditions: traffic volumes, crash rates, structural deficiency ratings, transit ridership, freight tonnage, delay times, or other relevant metrics - Explain the consequences of inaction — what happens if this project is not funded - Describe how the problem affects the local and regional transportation network - Identify the populations most affected, including any underserved, rural, or historically disadvantaged communities - Reference any prior studies, planning documents, or engineering analyses from {{content}} that document the need 3. PROJECT DESCRIPTION - Describe the proposed project in sufficient technical detail for reviewers to understand scope and complexity - Include: project type (construction, reconstruction, planning, design), key project elements, length/size/capacity, and major project components - Describe the project location with reference to major transportation corridors, interchanges, or facilities - Explain how the project addresses the stated need - Describe the project's relationship to the broader transportation network — connections to highways, transit, freight, ports, or other modes - If the project is multimodal, describe each modal component and how they integrate - Reference any design standards, engineering specifications, or technical requirements from {{content}} 4. PROJECT HISTORY AND DEVELOPMENT STATUS - Describe the history of project planning and development - Identify completed planning, environmental, or engineering work from {{content}} - Note the current project development phase (planning, NEPA, design, right-of-way, construction-ready) - Describe any prior federal, state, or local investments in the project or corridor - Identify any project partners — state DOT, MPO, transit agency, port authority, railroad, private sector — and their roles 5. APPLICANT QUALIFICATIONS AND CAPACITY - Describe the lead applicant's experience managing federal transportation grants - Reference prior BUILD, INFRA, TIGER, or other federal grant awards from {{content}} if applicable - Identify key project staff and their relevant experience - Describe the applicant's financial management systems and grant administration capacity - Note any technical assistance relationships with state DOT or other partners 6. COMMUNITY CONTEXT AND SUPPORT - Describe the community served by the project — population, geography, economic characteristics - Identify any rural, tribal, or historically disadvantaged community designations that apply - Describe community engagement conducted to date and level of public support - List letters of support, resolutions, or endorsements from elected officials, community organizations, or project partners referenced in {{content}} - Describe how the project aligns with local and regional planning documents (comprehensive plans, long-range transportation plans, freight plans) WRITING GUIDELINES: - Write for DOT program staff reviewers who evaluate hundreds of applications — be specific, quantitative, and concise - Every factual claim should be traceable to {{content}} or clearly labeled as a projection - Use plain language accessible to non-technical reviewers while maintaining technical accuracy - Do NOT fabricate project data, cost estimates, or community statistics not found in {{content}} - If {{content}} does not provide sufficient detail for a subsection, note what additional information from the applicant would strengthen it - Avoid jargon — spell out all acronyms on first use - Emphasize local and regional significance — BUILD prioritizes projects with significant local or regional impact BUILD PROGRAM CONTEXT: - BUILD grants range from $1M (rural) to $25M per project - 20% non-federal match required (flexibility for rural areas, persistent poverty areas, historically disadvantaged communities) - Eligible applicants: states, local governments, tribes, transit agencies, port authorities, special purpose districts - Projects must be surface transportation infrastructure (road, bridge, transit, rail, port, intermodal) - At least 1% of funds directed to historically disadvantaged communities or persistent poverty areas OUTPUT FORMAT: Generate well-structured HTML: - Use
